items.q: The printed pathogenesis of the overfill theory runs in which order?
opts: β hemolytic streptococci → releases plasmin → activates ENaC → 1° RAS activation → retention of Na+ and water
β hemolytic streptococci → activates ENaC → releases plasmin → 2° RAS activation → diuresis
Releases plasmin → β hemolytic streptococci → 1° RAS activation → ENaC blockade
ANP resistance → plasmin release → ENaC activation → 1° RAS activation
items.exp: Overfill theory, seen in nephritic syndrome: 1. β hemolytic streptococci releases plasmin → activates epithelial sodium channel (ENaC) → 1° RAS activation → retention of Na+, water (intravascular edema); 2. ANP resistance. (Book p758)

items.q: The overfill pathway is labelled with PRIMARY RAS activation, in contrast to the SECONDARY activation written in the underfill chart.
opts: True — the intravascular oedema of overfill arises without a preceding volume loss
False — both charts print primary RAS activation
False — overfill lists no RAS step at all
True — and overfill also lists a fall in effective circulatory volume
items.exp: p757 underfill ends in ↓ effective circulatory volume → 2° RAS activation; p758 overfill goes ENaC → 1° RAS activation → Na+/water retention (Intravascular edema), with ANP resistance as the second mechanism. (Book p758)

items.q: Fill up: In the overfill chain, the streptococcal product that activates the epithelial sodium channel is ______.
items.exp: The arrows read: β hemolytic streptococci → Releases plasmin → Activates epithelial sodium channel (ENaC). (Book p758)

items.q: Which pair is written in the third management box as 'Rare'?
opts: IgA nephropathy and minimal change disease
items.exp: The management row has three boxes: MCD (85–90%, steroid responsive 95%, no role of biopsy), FSGS (genetic form unresponsive to steroid; Rx renal transplantation) and membranous nephropathy (MN), IgA: Rare. (Book p758)
